correctness.rationale: For q>=2 an isomorphism class of a colour-partitioned bijection is exactly a multiset of directed q-colour necklaces, with Euler product ∏(1-z^d)^(-N_q(d)); Burnside gives N_q(d)=q^d/d+O(d q^(d/2)). Taking logarithms isolates H_q(z)/(1-qz), with H analytic and nonzero for |z|<q^(-1/2), so u_{n-s}/u_n=q^(-s)+exponentially small error. Marking finitely many specified necklaces gives independent geometric limits (1-q^(-d))q^(-jd) and rational capped-multiplicity event limits. For each local colour word v of radius R, necklaces deficient in T occurrences grow at exponential base beta<q by disjoint-block binomial bound; the multiset Euler product for deficient components converges beyond 1/q, proving exponential saturation of all long-cycle local types. Bounded-degree Hanf threshold locality then reduces any fixed first-order sentence (with function graph translated to binary relation) to finitely many capped short-necklace multiplicities, proving rational limit with exponential error. Excluding n=0 from sampling is harmless; q=1 is explicitly prior, with slower partition-ratio convergence. Independent Burnside counts for q=2 d<=7 and exact coefficient ratios were checked; not substituted for locality theorem.
